units.translation: where in one apograph ἀρῆς [curse], which should be written ἀρᾶς [curse] with Paleius, but the scholiast knew both readings, who explains ἀρῆς [curse] by βλάβης [harm], "Αρης [Ares]" however because Ἄρης ύπερμαχεῖ αὐτῶν καὶ οὐδὲν πάσχουσι διὰ τὸ σέβας τῶν θεῶν, ἄρος [Ares fights on their behalf and they suffer nothing because of their reverence for the gods, a defense] Ahrensius conjectured, which would be most fitting, unless ῥῦμα [defense] followed, nor can φυγάσιν [for the exiles] be separated by punctuation from τειρομένοις [for the oppressed], with which it clearly coheres.
The curse of father Cronus will then be utterly fulfilled.
Now indeed the curses of the father are fulfilled.
For the heavy reconciliations of the curses spoken long ago are complete (ἀραι without accent M, which Engerus corrected).
And upon her children she hurled curses (thus Hermannus for τέκνοις δ᾽ ἀραίας [for the children, curses]) of wrathful nurture, alas, bitter-tongued curses.
Ares, making the paternal curse (thus Bothius for πατρός [of the father]) true.
He pays the debt of the people's curse.
You have brought this sacrifice and have paid the curses of the people.
Setting the kick of the feast as a curse with justice.
Curses hurled by the people, stoning curses.
These things I place in the midst of the evil curse, telling them this evil curse.
Do you not revere the curses of your birth, child?
Averter of ruin
and to ward off ruin and destruction
And for those oppressed by war, the altar of Ares is a defense for exiles, the reverence of the gods,
